questions.q: According to the five-step flow for applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map, what comes immediately after 'Classifications found'?
options: Register asset
Labels applied
Scan asset
Create labels
questions.explain: The flow is: Create labels → Register asset → Scan asset → Classifications found → Labels applied. Classifications found is the trigger condition that leads directly to labels being applied.

questions.q: Does scanning a source apply a sensitivity label directly?
options: Yes, every scan automatically applies every published label
No — scanning only produces classifications; a separate auto-labeling policy is what actually applies the label
Yes, but only for Azure SQL Database sources
No, labels can only ever be applied manually, one asset at a time
questions.explain: The scan itself never applies a label directly — it produces classifications. A separate auto-labeling policy is what watches for those classifications and attaches the label.

questions.q: What scope must a sensitivity label have before it can be selected in an auto-labeling policy targeting Data Map sources?
options: Groups & sites
Meetings only
Files & other data assets
No scope is required
questions.explain: Only labels with the Files & other data assets scope can be selected for an auto-labeling policy that targets non-Microsoft 365 locations like Data Map sources.

questions.q: What kind of classifiers can an auto-labeling policy for non-Microsoft 365 workloads use as trigger conditions?
options: Only custom sensitive information types
Only trainable classifiers
Microsoft's prebuilt, out-of-the-box classifiers — custom SITs and trainable classifiers aren't supported here
Any classifier type, with no restrictions
questions.explain: Auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft 365 workloads can use Microsoft's prebuilt classifiers as conditions. Custom sensitive info types, named entities, trainable classifiers, credentials, and Exact Data Match are not supported for this policy type.

questions.q: Where can you find assets in the Unified Catalog by the sensitivity label applied to them?
options: Only by opening each asset individually and checking one by one
Through the search results' Label filter option
Labels are not searchable in the catalog at all
Only through a separate PowerShell script
questions.explain: The Unified Catalog's search results page includes a Label filter, alongside source type, classification, contact, and glossary term filters, letting you find all assets carrying a specific label.
